issues.description: Element: UML class name in the problem statement. The UML fragment in problem_statement.md declares the class as 'Course' (line 63: "class Course {"), while the template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 3) and the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 3) declare and use the class name 'Lecture'. This identifier mismatch between the UML and the actual code artifacts can confuse students about which class name to implement and refer to when mapping UML attributes to the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the UML class in problem_statement.md from 'Course' to 'Lecture' so the diagram matches the textual description and the provided code. Specifically, change the UML line 'class Course {' to 'class Lecture {' and leave the attribute names unchanged. This keeps the UML consistent with the template and solution and avoids confusing students about the expected class name.

issues.description: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares a class named 'Course' (identifier: Course) while the exercise text and both code artifacts define and refer to 'Lecture' (identifier: Lecture). Problem statement text (line 3) instructs students to implement a lecture class named 'Lecture', template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java declares 'public class Lecture', and the solution file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java also declares 'public class Lecture'. This mismatch (UML: Course vs. text/code: Lecture) can confuse students about which class to implement or test against, increasing cognitive load and risking them searching for or implementing a 'Course' class that does not exist in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifiers consistent: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare 'class Lecture { ... }' (replace the 'class Course' declaration with 'class Lecture' and keep the listed attributes and methods unchanged), so the UML matches the exercise text and the template/solution. Alternatively, if 'Course' was intentional, rename the template and solution classes and related references from 'Lecture' to 'Course' throughout the repository — but prefer updating the UML to 'Lecture' to preserve the current code and exercise text.
